title: Sharp macroscopic blow-up behavior for the parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system in dimensions $n\ge 3$
summary: We study the space-time concentration or blow-up asymptotics of radially decreasing solutions of the parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system in the whole space or in a ball. We show that, for any solution in dimensions $3\le n\le 9$ (assuming finite mass in the whole space case), there exists a nonflat backward self-similar solution $U$ such that $$u(x,t)=(1+o(1))U(x,t),\quad\hbox{as $(x,t)\to (0,T)$.}$$ This macroscopic behavior is important from the physical point of view, since it gives a sharp description of the concentration phenomenon in the scale of the original space-time…
